caption: Newanforbi v. Federal Express Corporation, E.D. Cal. 2:26-cv-02881-DAD-SCR
note: Private. Proof map and valuation for settlement only. Never attach, quote, or paraphrase in anything defense counsel sees. Probabilities are Plaintiff's working estimates: change them here and rerun `npm run valuation -- --matter 25`.

evidence.label: FedEx Answer (Dkt. 4) ¶ 26
evidence.quote: Defendant further admits that the adverse action letter referenced a review of the National Sex Offender Public Website and the California state Sex Offender website

evidence.label: FedEx Answer (Dkt. 4) ¶ 34
evidence.quote: the background screening report prepared by First Advantage and provided to FedEx identified Plaintiff as a registrant on California's sex offender registry

evidence.label: FedEx Answer (Dkt. 4), Seventh Affirmative Defense
evidence.quote: Defendant withdrew the conditional offer of employment based, independently and in part, on Plaintiff's dishonesty and material misrepresentations in his background check forms
evidence.why_reserve: 'in part' concedes the registry information was also part of the decision. Use it in mediation or in reply to the misrepresentation defense, not in the opening letter.

evidence.label: Notice of Removal (Dkt. 1) ¶¶ 28-29: FedEx's own wage math
evidence.quote: Twenty hours per week at $20.25 per hour equates to $405 in earnings per week ... 127-weeks of lost wages, which is approximately $51,435 ... an additional $42,120 in wages
evidence.why: Memo § 4A: present the figures as Plaintiff's own valuation; the match with their filing is recognized without citing it.

evidence.label: Bow Decl. (Dkt. 1-2) ¶ 6 and Ex. 9: pay range
evidence.quote: paid at an hourly rate ranging from $20.25-$21.25 for up to 20 hours of work per week
evidence.why_reserve: Held-back reserve (memo § 4A): the high end of their own pay range ($21.25 by May 2026) if the figure is called high.

evidence.label: First Advantage pre-adverse (Mar. 10, 2025) and adverse (Mar. 19, 2025) notices
evidence.pin: Mar. 10 and Mar. 19, 2025 emails from DoNotReply@fadv.com, 'for FEDEX GROUND HR'
evidence.quote: Please review the Adverse Action notification for your background screening report for FEDEX GROUND HR
evidence.why: Proves timing (nine days) and that First Advantage acted for FedEx. The notices do not show the report's contents; the portal links are expired.

evidence.label: First Advantage report and FedEx adjudication record
evidence.pin: RFP Set One; Rule 45 subpoena to First Advantage (Atts. A and B)
evidence.why: Shows the registry-source line and how FedEx adjudicated it. Set One and the subpoena are drafted but not yet served.

evidence.label: Jan. 8, 2025 background check forms (the 'NO' answer)
evidence.pin: RFP Set One no. 18 and the 'material application misrepresentation' requests
evidence.why: FedEx's main defense rests on the exact question asked and the answer given. Value moves most on this document.

elements.element: Registry information was used in the employment decision
elements.note: FedEx admits the adverse-action letter referenced both registry websites and the report identified Plaintiff as a registrant. It contests only that the use was unlawful.

elements.element: Adverse action: conditional offer withdrawn Mar. 19, 2025
The registry information caused the denial
elements.note: FedEx says the 'NO' answer was an independent basis. Its own words are 'independently and in part'.
Rate and hours come from FedEx's own filing. Interim earnings since Mar. 2025 reduce back pay; know Plaintiff's figure before sending.
No records yet. Plaintiff's testimony only. FedEx pleads none suffered (15th) and outside causes (16th).

defenses.name: Material misrepresentation / independent basis (6th, 7th, 11th, 14th)
open_questions: Exactly what the Jan. 8, 2025 form asked, and whether the answer was false as worded
Whether that question was a lawful inquiry at that stage of hiring (evaluate before relying on it)
Why the answer says the application was 'January 2025' when the file shows a July 17, 2024 application

defenses.name: Statutory exception: protection of persons at risk (8th)
open_questions: Whether FedEx can show any person-at-risk assessment beyond the conviction category

defenses.name: Avoidable consequences (17th)
open_questions: Plaintiff's interim earnings and job search since Mar. 19, 2025

damages.label: Back pay, Mar. 19, 2025 to trial (127 wks × $405)
damages.why_p: Rate is FedEx's own; the misrepresentation defense and interim earnings are the discount.

damages.label: Front pay, 104 wks after trial
damages.why_p: Speculative, and cut hardest if the misrepresentation defense holds.

damages.label: Pen. Code § 290.46(j)(4)(A) civil penalty (up to $25,000)
damages.why_p: Registry use is admitted; the 8th-defense exception is the risk. It is a cap, not a floor.

damages.label: Punitive (Civ. Code §§ 1786.50(b), 3294)
damages.why_p: Needs willful or grossly negligent conduct; nothing yet shows FedEx knew the use was barred.

positions.opening_basis: § 4A engine on FedEx's own wage math ($193,555, rounded); offer letter dated Sep. 25, 2026

trigger.label: Report ties the denial to a California-registry source (memo § 4)
trigger.note: FedEx's own answer already admits the adverse letter cited the registry websites and the report identified registration. The memo's 'after trigger' band applies now, not after the report.

repricing_events.if_favorable: Question was vague, unlawful at that stage, or the answer was not false as worded: raise back_pay and front_pay p.
repricing_events.if_unfavorable: Clear question and false answer: lower back_pay and front_pay p; penalty is unaffected.

repricing_events.event: First Advantage report and adjudication record produced
repricing_events.if_favorable: Registry line is the stated or only disqualifier: raise penalty and punitive p.
repricing_events.if_unfavorable: FedEx relied on the form answer first: lower causation-dependent lines.

repricing_events.if_favorable: A settlement conference date with Judge Riordan sets the clock for the next number.
